outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Limitations of Tokenization and the Case for Raw Bytes
outline.description: The contemporary landscape of Large Language Models (LLMs) is defined by a near-universal reliance on tokenization as a foundational pre-processing step. While modern architectures are increasingly trained end-to-end, the transition from raw digital data—streams of binary bytes—to the discrete units consumed by the model remains a heuristic bottleneck. Almost exclusively, strings are compressed into a finite set of tokens through algorithms like Byte Pair Encoding (BPE). This process groups bytes into sub-word units based on statistical frequency, creating a fixed vocabulary that serves as the interface between raw data and the neural network. outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: From Bytes to Patches – Strategies for Dynamic Grouping
outline.description: In the landscape of modern Large Language Models (LLMs), the transition from raw data to meaningful units of computation has historically been governed by a rigid, heuristic process known as tokenization. Traditional architectures rely on a fixed vocabulary, grouping raw bytes into a finite set of tokens before the model ever sees the data. This pre-processing step, while computationally convenient, imposes a static structure on the input that often fails to align with the actual complexity of the information being processed. The Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) challenges this paradigm by introducing a fundamentally different approach: patching. outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Architectural Deep Dive – The Three-Part BLT System
outline.description: The Byte Latent Transformer ({\textsc BLT}) represents a fundamental shift in Large Language Model (LLM) architecture by abandoning the rigid, fixed-vocabulary constraints of traditional tokenization. Instead of forcing raw byte sequences into a predetermined set of discrete symbols, {\textsc BLT} introduces a flexible, dynamic system capable of processing raw data directly while maintaining computational efficiency through a novel tripartite structure.
